title: Metadata Harvesting
summary: Automatically extract technical, operational and lineage metadata from source systems, pipelines and tools into a central metadata repository on a schedule or event basis.
body_markdown:
# Metadata Harvesting

## Problem

Manually maintained catalogs are incomplete and outdated.

## Context

Heterogeneous landscapes with databases, pipelines and BI tools.

## Forces

- Automation breadth vs. metadata depth (business meaning cannot be harvested).

## Solution

Connectors read schemas, job definitions, query logs and run events; normalise into the repository's metamodel; link harvested technical assets to curated business metadata (concepts, owners).

## Architecture

```text
DBs / pipelines / BI → connectors → normalise (metamodel) → metadata repository → catalog UI / API
                                                          ↖ curated business metadata
```

## Advantages

- Current technical metadata and lineage at low marginal cost.

## Disadvantages

- Connector coverage gaps; lineage through custom code is hard.

## Risks

- A catalog full of harvested but unexplained assets ("metadata swamp").

## When to Use

- More than a handful of systems; lineage required.

## When Not to Use

- Very small landscapes where curated documentation suffices.

## Alternatives

Manual curation; metadata-driven development (generate pipelines from metadata).

## Examples

- Nightly harvest of warehouse schemas plus runtime lineage events from orchestration.

## Related Decisions

- None yet; candidate decision "Metadata Architecture" (see recommended next batch).
